content.comment_body: Hello, I've just installed [product_name] version [version_no]. When starting a new diagram and using a mathematical instruction block in FBD view, there doesn't seem to be a Reference button for V1...V4 inputs. However, when I switch the diagram to LAD view, the Reference button appears. Has anyone else experienced this issue?
Same question as above. Same solution as previously mentioned :-)

Hello [user_name], The reference feature in FBD view is still available, but its interface has changed. Now, under the block you wish to reference, there is a plus sign. Clicking the plus sign lets you draw a connecting line; clicking again closes the reference blocks, leaving only a dashed line.

You're correct, thanks! I looked for similar posts but was searching specifically for something related to the REFERENCE button. I still think the software has a bug; the button should be visible. It's available in LAD view, but not in FBD.
If the reference button appears grey, it means there isn't a block in your program that can connect to the reference. Try placing an analog amplifier or a counter within your program.
OK, I understand now. In FBD view, only the 'plus' sign is implemented for this operation. Thank you.
My intention was to reference an up/down counter from a mathematical instruction or from an analog multiplexer.
Hello [user_name], Here are examples for both methods.

Hi! Why isn't it working as expected? Yesterday, my [product_name] software functioned differently; today, the reference option is missing. Finding this post helped, but I still don't understand why the feature cannot be used as previously.
The screenshot shows how I used to utilize the reference button in FBD view. I simply clicked on it and selected the desired option, without needing to draw lines, which made it simpler.
For more information, review this FAQ: How can you configure references between blocks in [product_name] [version_no]? [url]

analysis.insight_summary: The users experienced confusion about the visibility of the Reference button in the FBD editor of [product_name] [version_no]. While the option is clear in LAD view, FBD uses a new system with a plus sign, which led to difficulties for those familiar with previous designs. The shift in interface elements has caused uncertainty, particularly among users with prior experience of older software versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the referencing functionality to be easily accessible and clearly visible in both FBD and LAD views, with consistent interface elements for similar tasks.
